digest.component_or_area: S3 remote store healing and reconciliation
propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref in S3, git ls-remote returns the ref at two SHAs causing clone to fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed' and making the store unclonable.
git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects all writes while len(bundles) > 1, and rebar's retry loop cannot converge because the fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, stalling the push indefinitely.

Upstream git-s3 doctor is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts that crash on EOF) and by default discards non-chosen heads to orphan refs, causing irreversible loss of unique ticket events from the append-only event log.

The multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence hidden at the bundle-storage layer and reducible to the already-solved git case via lossless N-head 2-parent merge (reusing sync._union_merge semantics), followed by S3 write-then-delete to collapse bundles.
The doctor must write the merged bundle before deleting originals and never delete the merged result, ensuring at least one bundle with full merged history survives any crash point.

Concurrent repairs by N processes must serialize via the helper's per-ref lock; exactly one doctor merges and the rest back off, converging on the winner's collapsed remote without self-healing or corruption.
